claim.why_it_matters: The CURRENT-DATE character-position table is broken: the column header is plain text outside the table, the table ends after row 13-14, the 13-14 dash sub-items are detached outside the table, and rows 15-16, 17, 18-19 and 20-21 become loose paragraphs. Row 15-16 is further split mid-sentence so '99. The value 00 is returned...' stands as a separate paragraph detached from its position label. All words are present; the table structure that ties each content description to its character positions is lost.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 653 (PDF p677) shows one two-column table, header 'Character Positions' / 'Contents', with rows 1-4 through 20-21; the two em-dash LEAP-SECOND sub-items sit inside the 13-14 Contents cell, and row 15-16 reads continuously '...in the range 00 through 99. The value 00 is returned...'. page-677.md has the header as indented plain text outside the table, a markdown table holding only rows 1-4 to 13-14, the dash sub-items as a separate paragraph after the table, rows 15-16, 17, 18-19 and 20-21 as indented loose paragraphs, and row 15-16 broken by a blank line before '99\. The value 00...', so that sentence is a paragraph with no position label. The claim quotes both sources correctly. Every word is present and each loose row still begins with its position number, so no normative meaning changes. The table structure is still broken and one row's text is split across paragraphs, so this is a genuine structural defect, as the claim describes.
